course_outline_concepts: The operational loop every synthetic pipeline is an instance of: generate -> filter -> dedup -> verify -> select -> mix
Where each real pipeline (Self-Instruct, Nemotron-4, APIGen, OpenMathInstruct-2) sits in that loop
Why the loop is the right unit of analysis: it lets you port techniques between modalities
Failure mode per step: generation collapses to templates, filter over-prunes, dedup loses diversity, no verifier means no signal, selection biases the mix
The design-pattern lens is how the rest of this track will be taught - individual papers become cases, not doctrines

sources.what_to_extract: Four-step pipeline (seed -> instruction -> instance -> filter); 175 seed tasks; ROUGE-L > 0.7 diversity filter; 52K instructions / 82K instances from 252K raw generations; classification-vs-non-classification branching as the first quality gate; the bootstrap-from-LM-outputs template that every later SFT pipeline copies.

98% synthetic alignment data; 20K human anchor examples; reward-model-as-filter and reward-model-as-judge; Genetic Instruct for code; staged SFT (code SFT -> general SFT); DPO then RPO; output shape 800K code + 200K general + 160K DPO + 300K RPO; how a small human anchor set supports a large synthetic corpus.

3-layer verification (format -> execution -> semantic); 3,673 executable APIs; 60K accepted samples; ~40% rejection rate; ablation numbers (removing semantic -6%, execution -11%, format -18% on BFCL-V1); MinHash dedup on (query, call); how execution verification shrinks hallucination to <3%.

14M math CoT traces from Llama-3.1-405B; K=32 solutions per augmented problem at temp 1.0 top-p 0.95; SymPy symbolic equivalence as the verifier; question augmentation (paraphrase + novel-question) for diversity; 7% false-positive reasoning rate; teacher-strength ablation (405B at 1M beats Mixtral at 10M).

Verification is the bottleneck, not generation; easy-open-ended vs hard-verifiable split; prompt curation as a distinct cost-bearing stage; accumulation + verification over pure self-distillation; judge-LLM bias as the audit frontier.

Synthetic data as a family of augmentation and generation methods, not a single trick; rewrite / backtranslate / bootstrap / full-generate taxonomy; diversity vs faithfulness vs noise tradeoff per method.

Rephrased vs pure-generated scaling split; ~30% synthetic share as an empirical optimum for rephrased corpora; 5-10x speedup at fixed validation loss at large budgets; why textbook-style pure-generated collapses at scale while rephrase-style does not; prompt design is a first-class axis.
